# Bank Sector and Equal-Weight Market Analysis

Report 129 | Published 2024-02-04 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-2-4/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/129.json)

Bank dispersion and tentative cyclical recovery.

Egypt's near-term devaluation call resolved clearly, and the earlier AXP thesis performed well over its first three years. The new AXP horizon remains open. Equal weight lagged SPY in the chosen two-year sensitivity, whereas Chinese equities rebounded. The FDI annual-negative statement confuses definitions or periods. Bank-credit analysis correctly emphasized dispersion, but systemwide capital data do not verify every individual-bank exposure claim. Swan mining guidance remains unverified as an operating outcome and carries a disclosed board-role conflict.

**Coverage:** All numbered source blocks and chart labels read. All material macro, digital-asset and investment theses are reviewed. Routine holdings lists, incidental statistics and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Framework lessons

- Follow turning points while checking balance-sheet concentration.

## Verification limitations

- Retrieved November 7, 2026; the current webpage is not authenticated as the original publication-date wording.
- Chart labels were read but pixels and proprietary indicator vintages were not inspected.
- Adjusted-close evidence is a vendor proxy for reinvested distributions and splits, in USD without fees or taxes. It does not reconstruct actual portfolio trades. Chosen sensitivity windows are not author deadlines. Macro series use latest vintages.
